newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends strong as C Bank keeps rate.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends strong as C Bank keeps rate.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended higher on Monday as it drew strength from the Central Bank's high overnight borrowing rate which was kept at 15 percent, traders said.
Late last week, the Central Bank had to lift its key rate by 2.25 percentage points to 15 percent to fend off speculation arising from the problems of the Thai baht.
The peso closed at 26.373 from 26.380, with the day's average at 26.374 from 26.381. Volume was lower at $280.2 million from $397.7 million.
"They (the Central Bank) are observing how Thailand events will unfold," a foreign bank dealer said.
"The 15 percent overnight rate may be kept for the rest of the week," he added.
Traders said the Central Bank was both a buyer and seller of dollars in the market.

The Central Bank initially sold $49 million to $53 million for delivery today after some banks panicked, thinking the Central Bank may stay away from the market because of the holiday in the city of Manila.
Later, the Central Bank bought back about $55 million for settlement the next day at the rates of 26.373/26.373 as dollars flowed into the market, traders said.
